title: ASAN: `memcpy-param-overlap` in `font_cache_pool::font()`
description:
Hi,

CRAN's ASAN memtests started flagging my package, but the report points into ragg's vendored AGG rather than into my code, so I'm passing it along.

[clang-asan-00check.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31340092/clang-asan-00check.log.txt)
[gcc-asan-00check.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31340093/gcc-asan-00check.log.txt)

In both, `checking examples` and `checking tests` pass; only vignette re-building fails, once per vignette. Abridged from the clang run:

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: memcpy-param-overlap:
  memory ranges [0x7c29a562a440,0x7c29a562a538) and
                [0x7c29a562a448,0x7c29a562a540) overlap
  #1 agg::font_cache_pool::font(char const*, bool)
     agg/include/agg_font_cache_manager.h:176:21
  #2 agg::font_cache_manager<...>::synchronize()   :387
  #3 agg::font_cache_manager<...>::glyph(unsigned) :289
  #4 TextRenderer<...>::plot_glyphs(...)  text_renderer.h:461
  #5 AggDevice<...>::drawGlyph(...)       AggDevice.h:1549
  #6 agg_glyph<AggDevicePng<...>>(...)    init_device.h:370
  #7 GEGlyph                              R engine.c:3974
  #8 renderGlyphs / L_glyph               grid typeset.c:92/109

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: memcpy-param-overlap
  agg/include/agg_font_cache_manager.h:176:21 in agg::font_cache_pool::font(char const*, bool)
```

`gcc-ASAN` gives the identical summary:

```
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: memcpy-param-overlap
  agg/include/agg_font_cache_manager.h:176 in agg::font_cache_pool::font(char const*, bool)
```

When the font cache pool is full and another font is requested, the eviction path shifts the array down with `memcpy`:

```cpp
// src/agg/include/agg_font_cache_manager.h:173
if(m_num_fonts >= m_max_fonts)
{
    obj_allocator<font_cache>::deallocate(m_fonts[0]);
    std::memcpy(m_fonts,
           m_fonts + 1,
           (m_max_fonts - 1) * sizeof(font_cache*));
    m_num_fonts = m_max_fonts - 1;
}
```

`m_fonts` and `m_fonts + 1` are the same array one element apart, so the ranges overlap and this is undefined behaviour. It wants `memmove`.

Potential fix would be 
```diff
-                    std::memcpy(m_fonts,
+                    std::memmove(m_fonts,
                            m_fonts + 1,
                            (m_max_fonts - 1) * sizeof(font_cache*));
```

`memmove` is already what the same vendored tree uses for this kind of overlapping shift, e.g. `src/agg/include/agg_array.h:309`. This comes from upstream AGG 2.4.

Happy to open a PR if it is easier.

title: Perhaps add a SIXEL output device?
description: Hi, I implemented a SIXEL output device based on ragg's rendering pipeline and would like to ask whether this would be a good fit for ragg. The motivation is remote R usage over SSH. X11 forwarding works, but becomes quite slow for complex plots, and terminal emulators with SIXEL support provide a convenient way to display raster graphics directly in the terminal. Example output: The device renders through AGG and encodes the resulting raster image as SIXEL. It is implemented with a small header-only C++ SIXEL encoder and does not add a dependency on libsixel. I have been using this locally for several months for my SSH + R workflow and it has been stable. I would like to know whether this kind of output target is within ragg's scope. Thanks!

title: agg_png renders blank PNG for grid.text + Calibri at certain font sizes (7.5, 8.0, 8.5, 9.5 pt) on Windows
description:
When rendering text in **Calibri** to `ragg::agg_png` at certain fractional font sizes between roughly 6 and 10 pt, the entire PNG comes out blank (white) — silently, with no warning or error. The bug is **independent of `ggplot2`** (reproducible with `grid::grid.text` alone) and the pattern is erratic by font size.

## Minimal reproducible example

```r
library(ragg); library(grid)
agg_png("blank.png", width = 6, height = 3.7, units = "in", res = 150)
grid.text("Hello",
          gp = gpar(fontfamily = "Calibri", fontsize = 8))
dev.off()

file.info("blank.png")$size
#> [1] 2850   # blank 906x559 white PNG (no text visible)
```

## Font size sweep (Calibri, `grid.text`, `agg_png` at `res = 150`)

| `fontsize` | Result |
|---|---|
| 6.0 | **BLANK** |
| 6.5 | BLANK |
| 7.0 | ok |
| 7.5 | **BLANK** |
| 8.0 | **BLANK** |
| 8.5 | **BLANK** |
| 9.0 | ok |
| 9.5 | **BLANK** |
| 10.0 | ok |
| 10.5 | ok |
| 11.0+ | ok |

The same pattern reproduces via ggplot2 (which was how I first hit it). With `theme_bw(base_size = 7, base_family = "Calibri") + labs(title = "Bug")`, the default `plot.title` size is `rel(1.2) × 7 = 8.4 pt` — squarely in the broken zone — so adding a title to any plot causes the whole rendered PNG to be blank.

## Control — Arial

Arial also exhibits blanks but at different sizes, suggesting this is a per-font glyph-rasterization issue (perhaps interaction with embedded bitmaps in Microsoft's TrueType files on Windows).

```r
# Arial at res=150 / grid.text:
#  size 7.0 -> BLANK
#  size 7.5 -> BLANK
#  size 8.0 -> ok
#  size 8.5 -> ok
#  size 9.0 -> ok
```

## Environment

- R 4.5.3 (Windows 11 Pro 26200, 64-bit)
- `ragg` 1.5.2
- `systemfonts` 1.3.2
- `ggplot2` 4.0.3 (for the ggplot variant — not needed to reproduce)
- Calibri TTF: `C:\Windows\Fonts\calibri.ttf`, `calibrib.ttf` (default Microsoft Office font)

`systemfonts::match_fonts("Calibri")` resolves correctly to the TTF files. The issue manifests at rasterization time, not at font lookup. No warning or message is emitted.

## Known workarounds

- `dpi = 96` or `dpi = 300` may produce different sweep patterns (not exhaustively tested).
- Use a different font family (`base_family = ""`, `"sans"`).
- Switch device: `grDevices::png(type = "cairo")` or `cairo_pdf` renders correctly with Calibri at these sizes.

Happy to provide additional traces (e.g. raster bitmap dumps, `systemfonts::font_info()` output, or a sweep across `res` values) if useful.

title: Certain characters replaced with emoji in rendered PNG/JPG files
description:
The annotation in the following plot shows the first character as a symbolic arrow character, which is contained in the font: ``` library(ggplot2) data.frame(x = c("a", "b", "c"), y = 1:3) |> ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_col() + annotate(geom = "text", x = "a", y = 2, label = "↙ Here") ```
However, when you `ggsave("reprex.png")` and look at _reprex.png_ (or, say, Quarto documents using `ragg_png`), the character is unexpectedly replaced by an emoji:
A quirk that makes me wonder whether this is intended behaviour: in the following real example that led me to stumble upon this issue, it is only the third annotation, where the annotation starts with the diagonal arrow, that the character is replaced by an emoji - the first two, that end in a straight arrow, are left as-is:
And, oddly, if you modify the reprex from earlier so that the label is simply `label = "↙"` instead of "↙ Here", then the plot is rendered without the emoji, even by `agg_png()`. It would be great if there were a way to predictably get the arrow character into the final plot without having to switch over to `grDevices::png` to get there. Out of curiosity, is this something that could possibly be made a user option like `auto_insert_emoji = FALSE` or something? For what it's worth, tested with: R version 4.5.3 Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu Running under: Fedora Linux 43 (Toolbx Container Image) ragg 1.5.2

title: Slow performance with large local font directory
description:
Calling requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE) can be very slow with a large local font directory.  This is run as part of the validate_device() function of ggplot2.

Looking through it seems like systemfonts::scan_local_fonts() and systemfonts:::add_local_fonts() are called, causing most of the delay when the local font directory is large.  Is it possible to cache a list of available local fonts and then load them as required?

title: agg_png renders plotmath %*% as centered dot (·) instead of multiplication sign (×)
description:
## Description

`ragg::agg_png` renders the plotmath `%*%` operator as a centered dot (· U+00B7) instead of the multiplication sign (× U+00D7). `grDevices::png` renders it correctly as ×.

**Expected:** `expression(italic(P) == 2.36 %*% 10^-05)` renders with × (multiplication sign)
**Actual:** The same expression renders with · (middle dot / centered dot) when using `agg_png`

## Minimal reprex

```r
library(ragg)

expr <- expression(italic(P) == 2.36 %*% 10^-05)

# ragg: %*% renders as centered dot (·)
agg_png("reprex_ragg.png", width = 400, height = 150, res = 150)
par(mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
plot.new()
title(main = "ragg::agg_png")
text(0.5, 0.5, expr, cex = 1.5)
dev.off()

# grDevices: %*% renders correctly as multiplication sign (×)
grDevices::png("reprex_grdevices.png", width = 400, height = 150, res = 150)
par(mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
plot.new()
title(main = "grDevices::png")
text(0.5, 0.5, expr, cex = 1.5)
dev.off()
```

Compare `reprex_ragg.png` (shows ·) with `reprex_grdevices.png` (shows ×).

## Session info

- R 4.5.2 (2025-10-31)
- Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (Linux)
- ragg 1.5.0

## Related issues

This may be related to other symbol/font rendering issues:

- #89
- #90
- #51

title: agg_record and agg_capture advance global RNG state, leading to unintuitive downstream behavior
description:
`ragg::agg_record()` and `ragg:agg_capture()` advance R’s global RNG state by calling `sample()` to generate a device name. This causes `.Random.seed` to change during graphics device initialization, etc. 

This arguably breaks reproducibility guarantees when these functions are used as infrastructure, for example by `IRkernel` in Jupyter notebooks.

# Minimal example

In a Jupyter / IRkernel context (but reproducible via direct calls):

```r
set.seed(1)
s1 <- .Random.seed

# Device initialization triggers RNG use
ragg::agg_record()
dev.off()

s2 <- .Random.seed
identical(s1, s2)
# FALSE
```

The RNG advance occurs here:

```r
paste0("agg_record_", sample(.Machine$integer.max, 1))
```
and here:
```r
paste0('agg_capture_', sample(.Machine$integer.max, 1))
```

on lines 430 and 507 of `agg_dev.R` (and potentially elsewhere?)

## Unintuitive behavior

- `agg_record()` is now used implicitly as a recording device (for example by IRkernel / evaluate in Jupyter notebooks)
- This causes `.Random.seed` to advance between notebook cells,  even for deterministic code
- Running the same code via `Rscript` does not exhibit this behavior
- This creates unintuitive differences between running code in a notebook versus converting the notebook to a script and running it, due solely to differences in RNG state

It is unclear whether this is an intentional design decision, and whether users should expect code to behave differently in a Jupyter notebook versus a script. However, this makes the placement of cell breaks in a notebook affect RNG state, which is quite unintuitive.

For example, a single cell:

```r
set.seed(1234)
runif(1)
```

behaves differently than two sequential cells:

```r
set.seed(1234)
```

```r
runif(1)
```

This is likely confusing for typical users.

## Environment

- ragg: 1.5.0
- IRkernel: 1.3.2
- R: 4.5.2

title: Introduce callback when plot is updated
description:
Would it be possible to introduce the option to specify a callback function in `ragg` that is called whenever the plot is updated? 

Use case: I am the author the `terminalgraphics` package (https://codeberg.org/djvanderlaan/terminalgraphics). To get that working I open a `agg_capture` device that receives the plot commands. I add a callback to R using `addTaskCallback`. That callback checks if the device has changed (the contents of that device) and dumps a new plot into the terminal when it has. I currently have an issue when the plot is updated but the contents of the plot do not change: then no change is detected and the plot is not updated. 

```R
plot(1:10)
# a lot of commands
# ...
plot(1:10)
# nothing happens as the contents of the device did not change
```

I imagine this could be either through a `ragg::register_callback` function (that probably receives the device that updated) or through an additional argument to `agg_capture` /`agg_png` etc. 

If time is an issue: I would be willing to dive into the code and try to make a pull request.

title: grDevices::windows function is broken when called from IRkernel; appears to be related to the ragg package
description:
I have a strange problem that manifests itself with a ```grDevices::windows()``` device when ragg is loaded from ```IRkernel```. The manifestation is that when the ```windows()``` function is called from an ```IRkernel``` prompt, the graphics device frame is shown, but there is no text in the menus. This only occurs within ```IRkernel``` and not from other terminals such as ```radian``` or from within  ```RStudio```.

To see a better description, please see IRkernel/IRkernel#751 which shows screenshots of the issue. Particularly, please see https://github.com/IRkernel/IRkernel/issues/751#issuecomment-3171876463 where I can make the graphics device show the menu text by removing the ```ragg``` library. I can load the ```systemfonts``` and ```textshaping``` libraries without any menu text issues. I am happy to repost details and screenshots here if that is helpful.

Having looked at the C code for ```grDevices```, I am not sure how to debug the cause of the issue since I don't have an R executable with debug symbols. My guess at this point is that somehow the fonts used by ```grDevices``` or the menu creation process is being blocked.

I am wondering if someone could help me run tests to get to the bottom of the issue?

title: Crash on macOS Sonoma 14.5 when saving PNG/TIFF with ggsave (ragg/systemfonts/textshaping)
description:
Summary
On macOS Sonoma 14.5 (ARM64, R 4.5.1), ggsave() with PNG or TIFF devices crashes the R session when {ragg, textshaping, systemfonts} are involved. This occurs even for trivial ggplot2 plots. pdf output works fine.

The crash trace shows a segfault in FreeType’s COLRv1 handling (tt_face_get_paint_layers), called from systemfonts → harfbuzz → textshaping → ragg during string width measurement. After reinstalling {ragg, textshaping, systemfonts} from CRAN binaries and explicitly using ragg::agg_png or ragg::agg_tiff, the problem was resolved.

Minimal reprex
```
library(ggplot2)

# Crashes
ggsave("test.png", ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) + geom_point())

# Works after reinstall + explicit ragg device
ggsave("test.png",
       ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) + geom_point(),
       device = ragg::agg_png, width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300)

ggsave("test.tiff",
       ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) + geom_point(),
       device = ragg::agg_tiff, width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300,
       compression = "lzw")
```

Crash log (truncated)
```
Exception Type:        EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Codes:       KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x000000000000004a

Thread 0 Crashed:
0   systemfonts.so      tt_face_get_paint_layers (ttcolr.c:1529)
1   libharfbuzz.0.dylib hb_ft_get_glyph_extents
2   textshaping.so      HarfBuzzShaper::fill_shape_info
3   ragg.so             textshaping::string_width
4   libR.dylib          GEStrWidth
5   grid.so             L_stringMetric
...
```

Environment
```
R version 4.5.1 (2025-06-13)
Platform: aarch64-apple-darwin20
Running under: macOS Sonoma 14.5

Packages:
- ragg 1.4.0
- systemfonts 1.2.3
- textshaping 1.0.1
- ggplot2 3.5.2
```
systemfonts::font_info("Helvetica") runs without issue.
ggsave(..., device = "pdf") always works.

Workarounds

Forcing Quartz device works:
```
ggsave("test.png", plot, device = function(...) grDevices::png(type = "quartz", ...))
```

Full fix: clean reinstall of {ragg, textshaping, systemfonts} from CRAN arm64 binaries. After that, ragg::agg_png and ragg::agg_tiff worked reliably.

title: Colorbar created with `legendry::guide_colbar` and `ggplot2::scale_color/fill_gradient2` not rendered correctly in version 1.4.0
description:
"Diverging" colorbars created with `legendry::guide_colbar` and `scale_color/fill_gradient2` are no longer rendered correctly in `ragg` version `1.4.0`, i.e. the "upper" part of the colorbar looks like a binned guide, whereas the "lower" one is fine. title: ragg installation in docker container
description:
We are trying to build a shiny app in a container environment that takes ragg package to render custom fonts. 

The docker build fails with the following message. 
Full build log here: [build_log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19605224/build_log.txt)

```
-----------------------------------------------------
FontDescriptor.h:7:10: fatal error: ft2build.h: No such file or directory
7 | #include <ft2build.h>
| ^~~~~~~~~~~~
compilation terminated.
make: *** [/usr/lib/R/etc/Makeconf:204: caches.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package âsystemfontsâ
* removing â/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/systemfontsâ
ERROR: dependency âsystemfontsâ is not available for package âtextshapingâ
* removing â/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/textshapingâ

* removing â/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/raggâ
*
-----------------------------------------------------
```

I have included all the system requirements as listed in the package description. Here is the full docker reproducible example.


```
FROM rocker/r-base:4.4.1

# Install dependencies for 'ragg'
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    libpng-dev \
    libtiff5-dev \
    libjpeg-dev \
    libfreetype6-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN R -e "install.packages('shiny', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/', dependencies=TRUE)"
RUN R -e "install.packages('ragg', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/', dependencies=TRUE)"


RUN echo "local(options(shiny.port = 3838, shiny.host = '0.0.0.0'))" > /usr/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site
RUN groupadd --system app && useradd --system --gid app app
WORKDIR /home/app
COPY app .

RUN chown app:app -R /home/app
USER app
EXPOSE 3838
```

title: UTF-8 characters in filename for `agg_png`
description:
I've noticed that `agg_png` doesn't handle UTF-8 in file names well.
## Example
``` r
library(ragg)

file <- "русское_название.png"
agg_png(file)
plot(sin, -pi, 2*pi)
dev.off()
```
Above code produces a file named `СЂСѓСЃСЃРєРѕРµ_РЅР°Р·РІР°РЅРёРµ.png` instead of `русское_название.png`, like `grDevices::png` would. If a path has a UTF-8 in folder names, device would fail to write with `agg could not write to the given file` error.

I've tried to wrap filename with `enc2native` or `enc2utf8`, but it doesn't seem to help.

Gives the error:
```

title: `saturate` compositing operator
description:
The only compositing operator supported by the Cairo devices that is not supported by `{ragg}` seems to be the "saturate" operator:

```r
ragg::agg_record()
ragg_cap <- dev.capabilities()
invisible(dev.off())
png(type = "cairo")
cairo_cap <- dev.capabilities()
invisible(dev.off()
pdf(file = NULL)
pdf_cap <- dev.capabilities()
invisible(dev.off())
```
```r
> setdiff(cairo_cap$compositing, ragg_cap$compositing)
[1] "saturate"
```

A description of the operator from: https://www.cairographics.org/operators/ 

> CAIRO_OPERATOR_SATURATE
> 
> The output of the SATURATE operator is the same for both bounded and unbounded source interpretations.
>
> | Resulting alpha (`aR`) | Resulting color (`xR`) |
> | - | - |
> | `min(1, aA+aB)` |	`(min(aA, 1−aB)·xA + xaB)/aR` |

title: Possible improvements w.r.t. `dev.capabilities()`
description:
* `dev.capabilities("transparentBackground")` for {ragg} devices seems to  always be `"fully"` (i.e. semi-transparent backgrounds are not supported and only fully transparent backgrounds are supported).

  + However some light testing suggests that `ragg::agg_png()` actually supports semi-transparent backgrounds and thus this should be `"semi"` instead for this device and any other `{ragg}` devices that support semi-transparent backgrounds.
  + In contrast I speculate `ragg::agg_ppm()` should be `"no"` since the documentation for `agg_ppm` suggests it is a 8bit RGB stream (i.e. no alpha channel support).  Also unsure about the extent of alpha channel support in `agg_jpeg()`.

* Currently `dev.capabilities("rasterImage")` for {ragg} devices seems to always be `NA`.  However, I think all of `{ragg}`'s graphics devices fully support drawing raster images as used by `rasterImage()` and `grid.raster()`
 
  + According to `?dev.capture` possible values are `"no"`, `"yes"`, and `"non-missing"` 
  + I speculate the actual support for the `rasterImage` capability by {ragg}'s graphics devices should be `"yes"`

* `dev.capabilities("capture")` for `agg_capture()` is currently `NA`.   However some light testing shows `ragg::agg_capture()` supports both `grid.cap()` and `dev.capture()`.  Thus I speculate this should instead be `TRUE` for the `agg_capture()` device.   Currently this seems to be `FALSE` for all the other {ragg} graphics devices (which seems to be correct).

```r
ragg::agg_png()
# ragg::agg_ppm() # same output as `ragg::agg_png()`
dev.capabilities(c("transparentBackground", "rasterImage"))
invisible(dev.off())
```
```r
$transparentBackground
[1] "fully"

$rasterImage
[1] NA
```
```r
ragg::agg_capture()
dev.capabilities("capture")
dev.off()
```
```r
$capture
[1] NA
```

title: Where and why does ragg changes the fonts on Linux systems?
description:
Hi, 

i noticed my plots look differentially when being hosted on shinyapps.io - running a linux system (compared to my local system) and was able to attribute this to the ragg-library. 
In some replies to other issues you say "Don't rely just on the font by supplied by the OS as results may look different". 
e.g.: https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/issues/124
However, to me it seems it is not just a Windows (or Mac) vs. Linux but ragg vs. png when on Linx issue. 

Here the first attempts to identify the problem:
https://community.rstudio.com/t/plots-on-shinyapps-io-are-rendered-differentially-depending-on-used-libraries/177636/3

You can see it even in your own explanation: https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2021/02/modern-text-features/
![grafik](https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/assets/70321724/c994ed25-39fb-4fc5-a049-5a744513c59d)

When looking at the titles, there is not a big difference between Windows - Mac - Linux, but the biggest difference is Linux-Cairo vs. Linux-ragg (more spacing between the letters, less weight - looks more like Plotly). 

Also this seems to strongly affect the fontfamily ("symbol") for mathematical expressions, as reported in
https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/issues/150
https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/issues/89
https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/issues/101

In my case the multiplcation symbol of an expression (%*%) is not working correctly and just presenting a dot (when being hosted on shinyapps.io and using ragg). Using '*' or using '×' is working fine, the same is true for saving plots with device = png or working on windows.

If the font in Linux doesn't support special characters, why is it working without ragg? At which point another font is defined? Is this driven by systemfonts? 

Example:
```
library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)
library(shiny)

# Define UI 
ui <- fluidPage(
    titlePanel("PlotRenderTest"),
    column(width = 6, imageOutput("Plot_png") ),
    column(width = 6, imageOutput("Plot_ragg") )
    )

# Define server logic 
server <- function(input, output) {
  
  # Base Plot
  Plot = reactive({
    ggplot(data = data.frame(x = c(1,2,3),
                             y = c(30, 10, 20)),
           aes(x = x, y = y)) + 
      geom_col() + theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = c(parse(text = "1*'*'*10"),
                                    parse(text = "2%*%10"),
                                    parse(text = "3*'×'*10")),
                         breaks = c(1,2,3))
  })

    # save plot as png
  output$Plot_png = renderImage({
    ggsave("Plot.png",
           device = png, 
      plot = Plot() + labs(title = "device = png"),
      bg = "white", dpi = 96, width=15, height = 13, units = "cm")

    # Return the filename for the download function 
    list(src = "Plot.png", contentType = 'image/png')
  }, deleteFile = FALSE)
  
  # save plot as ragg-png, 
  output$Plot_ragg = renderImage({
    ggsave("Plot_ragg.png",
           plot = Plot() + labs(title = "device = ragg"),
           bg = "white", dpi = 96, width=15, height = 13, units = "cm")

  # Return the filename for the download function 
    list(src = "Plot_ragg.png", contentType = 'image/png')
  }, deleteFile = FALSE)
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```
On Windows:
![grafik](https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/assets/70321724/afc312e5-3e16-4361-8e18-e1ef87df3ee3)

On shinyapps.io: 
![grafik](https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/assets/70321724/b8413b9e-99a2-42e7-962b-8cb8f4a8f56e) 

Summary: 
ragg on Linux (shinyapps.io) - different font, looks like plotly, special characters are sometimes broken. 
Linux without ragg - very similar to visual appearence in other operating systems.

title: rectangles ignore `linejoin` settings
description: Hi Thomas, In the new version of ragg, rectangles (not polygons in general) appear to ignore the `linejoin` setting. When specifying a rectangle with `linejoin = "mitre"`, I expected straight corners, but rounded corners show up. ``` r library(grid) tmp1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") tmp2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") draw_rect <- function() { grid.newpage() grid.rect( width = 0.5, height = 0.5, gp = gpar(lwd = 20, linejoin = "mitre") ) } ragg::agg_png(tmp1) draw_rect() dev.off() #> png #> 2 knitr::include_graphics(tmp1) ``` For reference how I expected the rectangle to look like: ``` r png(tmp2, type = "cairo-png") draw_rect() dev.off() #> png #> 2 knitr::include_graphics(tmp2) ``` Created on 2024-03-14 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)

title: R Session Aborted with ragg + ggdag (+ ggraph) + RStudio
description:
So, I don't know where to file this issue exactly because I think this is several bugs working in concert. However, when I use the AGG backend in RStudio, I encounter session ending crash when running simple ggdag code

```r
library(ggdag)
dag <- dagify(
  y ~ x + z2 + w2 + w1,
  x ~ z1 + w1,
  z1 ~ w1 + v,
  z2 ~ w2 + v,
  w1 ~~ w2,
  exposure = "x",
  outcome = "y"
)
ggdag_adjustment_set(dag)
```

Unfortunately, I can't replicate this with code using the ragg devices. However, I do not have a crash except when using it on RStudio and ragg on a Mac (e.g., I can't replicate in on Posit Cloud). However, I have had others be able to replicate it using those settings on their Macs. Everything works in the terminal and on CI checks, as well.

I do not really know the source of the bug, but it's got *something* to do with ggraph, and I think specifically to do with the cap-related code. ggdag uses ggraph in an unusual way, and it seems that in *faceted plots with caps on edges*, it is invoking some bug in ggraph that I can't replicate with true ggraph code (e.g. outside of ggdag). Then, this mystery bug is somehow getting caught up in the ragg-RStudio interface. That's as far as my detective skills have gotten me, and I'm not totally confident in that assessment.

I have experienced weird issues like this in the past but not conistently, and I've never been able to replicate them until now. I tried to install an old version of ragg but I'm having trouble compiling it, so I'm not sure if it's to do with recent versions or not.

I'm posting the issue here because of the confluence of ragg and ggraph, but also turning ragg on and off in RStudio was how I was finally able to replicate the issue. 

I have the most recent version of everything in question, and I've tried various configurations of RStudio and R builds.

description: Hi Thomas, I think I might have found a precision bug with linear gradients in {ragg}. I'm aiming to fill an object with a gradient flanked by two flat colours. Smugly pleased with myself, I imagined I could do this by using tiny increments in the `stops` argument of `grid::linearGradient()`. They do show up when I use `stops = c(0, 0.01, 0.99, 1)`. ``` r library(grid) grad <- linearGradient( colour = c("tomato", "white", "black", "dodgerblue"), stops = c(0, 0.0001, 0.9999, 1), y1 = 0.5, y2 = 0.5, x1 = unit(0.1, "npc"), x2 = unit(0.9, "npc"), ) rect <- rectGrob(gp = gpar(fill = grad)) tmp1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") tmp2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") ragg::agg_png(tmp1) grid.newpage() grid.draw(rect) dev.off() #> png #> 2 knitr::include_graphics(tmp1) ``` Drawing the same rectangle with the regular png device, it looks like I expected. ``` r png(tmp2, type = "cairo-png") grid.newpage() grid.draw(rect) dev.off() #> png #> 2 knitr::include_graphics(tmp2) ``` Created on 2024-01-06 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)

title: pkg-config errors and workaround
description:
Good morning, 

I was running into some installation challenges on my university's HPC system, and managed to find [a workaround](https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/compare/main...grantbrown:ragg:main) with a few small tweaks to the configure file. Broadly, I think there are two issues:

1. libjpeg should be in the list of things pkg-config should be looking for and providing compiler flags
2. There's some other error getting caught by $? that doesn't actually prevent successful compilation and installation of the package (previously it was getting dumped back out with exit 1 despite finding all the libraries needed). 

I'm not 100% sure what is causing that second issue, but perhaps glancing at the workaround can help someone with a deeper knowledge of pkg-config/R package builds. 

Hope this is useful to someone.

title: affine transformation feature
description:
* In the comments to https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/2314 @hadley asked me to open an issue here.
* The affine transformation feature was introduced in R 4.2.  Here is an article about it by Paul Murrell: https://www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/~paul/Reports/GraphicsEngine/groups/groups.html

           cfg = cfg, envir = envir, x = 1:7, y = 1,
           default.units = "in", op_scale = 0.5)

title: When linking with library flags generated by `pkg-config`, the `-ljpeg` flag is duplicated
description:
See discussion in #152 for more context. The short version is that duplicated link flags fails when building for webR/Wasm with Emscripten.

---

In the package's `configure` script, `pkg-config` is used to find `libjpeg`,

https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/blob/792c1e10fa0ebcd7d89ff3e5227f51e8d299ec82/configure#L8

but later, the `-ljpeg` flag is also manually appended,

https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/blob/792c1e10fa0ebcd7d89ff3e5227f51e8d299ec82/configure#L37-L39

If we are relying on `pkg-config` and the existence of `jpeg.pc`, can we remove the additional `-ljpeg`?

Alternatively, should https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/commit/fa87a16a1bd19ce2680ddc22ee3bd576e189ddd7 be reverted? The argument for that is that older versions of libjpeg did not install a `jpeg.pc` for `pkg-config` to use.

I don't particularly mind which of the two solutions we land on.

title: Issues with geom_tile()
description:
Hi, 

Lately, I have had issues using ragg (last version) with geom_tile(). I am not sure where it comes from, but using png_cairo on windows doesn't provoke this strange pattern, which I guess come from "colour". 

```
library(elevatr)
library(tidyverse)
library(raster)
library(ragg)

data(lake)

loc_df <- data.frame(x = runif(6,min=sp::bbox(lake)[1,1], 
                               max=sp::bbox(lake)[1,2]),
                     y = runif(6,min=sp::bbox(lake)[2,1], 
                               max=sp::bbox(lake)[2,2]))
# Example for PROJ > 5.2.0
r <- get_elev_raster(locations = loc_df, prj = sp::wkt(lake) , z=10)

r_xy <- as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
names(r_xy)[3] <- "elev"

# plot
g <- ggplot(r_xy, 
            aes(x, y, fill = elev)) +
      geom_tile() +
      theme_void()

#ragg 
agg_png("tile_ragg.png", 
        width = 5,

title: Prefer using PKG_CPPFLAGS for ragg headers
description:
From https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Using-Makevars:

> N.B.: Include paths are preprocessor options, not compiler options, and must be set in PKG_CPPFLAGS as otherwise platform-specific paths (e.g. ‘-I/usr/local/include’) will take precedence. PKG_CPPFLAGS should contain ‘-I’, ‘-D’, ‘-U’ and (where supported) ‘-include’ and ‘-pthread’ options: everything else should be a compiler flag. The order of flags matters, and using ‘-I’ in PKG_CFLAGS or PKG_CXXFLAGS has led to hard-to-debug platform-specific errors.

And also:

> Use #include "my.h" not #include <my.h> for headers in your package. The second form is intended for system headers and the search order for such headers is platform-dependent (and may not include the current directory). For extra safety, name headers in a way that cannot be confused with a system header so not, for example, types.h.

Because Makevars.in sets the include path via PKG_CXXFLAGS here:

https://github.com/r-lib/ragg/blob/f6acc4c89540a71743074455d5c93e7f48ff075e/src/Makevars.in#L1

we run the risk of picking up an alternate installation of `agg`, rather than the bundled version. It should suffice to just set the include paths in `PKG_CPPFLAGS` rather than updating how `agg` is included, though.

title: linemitre threshold
description:
Hi Thomas and team,

I just noticed that the ragg png and cairo png devices handle linemitre thresholds somewhat differently. This causes the cairo device to bevel the linejoins in the graphic below, whereas ragg does not. I'm no expert on the subject, but I had expected to see bevelled linejoins at `linemitre = 1` (the lower limit that {grid} accepts).

Thanks for reading!

``` r
library(grid)

grob <- polylineGrob(
  x = seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = 4),
  y = rep(c(0.1, 0.9), length.out = 4),
  gp = gpar(
    linemitre = 1, lwd = 20,
    linejoin = "mitre"
  )
)

tmp1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
png(tmp1, type = "cairo")
grid.newpage() 
grid.draw(grob)
dev.off()
#> png 
#>   2
knitr::include_graphics(tmp1)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/FTfh9ps.png)

``` r

tmp2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
ragg::agg_png(tmp2)
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(grob)
dev.off()
#> png 
#>   2
knitr::include_graphics(tmp2)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/EIohb0k.png)

title: "Tofu" when newline character is at the edge of character string
description:
The ragg png device produces a "tofu" symbol when there is a newline character (\n) at the beginning or the end of a text string.

This does not happen with the Cairo png device.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

#+ dev = "ragg_png"
ggplot() +
  geom_text(aes(x = 0, y = 0, label = "\n")) +
  labs(x = "\nat the beginning", y = "at the end\n")
```

``` r
#+ dev = "png", dev.args = list(type = "cairo-png")

title: macOS 11 arm64 homebrew configure file tweaks
description:
as per the twitter thread, I ended up having to tweak `PKG_CONFIG_NAME`, `PKG_BREW_NAME`, and `PKG_LIBS`:

```
# Library settings
PKG_CONFIG_NAME="freetype2 libpng libtiff-4 webp harfbuzz"
PKG_DEB_NAME="libfreetype6-dev libpng-dev libtiff5-dev libjpeg-dev"
PKG_RPM_NAME="freetype-devel libpng-devel libtiff-devel libjpeg-turbo-devel"
PKG_CSW_NAME="libfreetype_dev libpng16_dev libtiff_dev libjpeg_dev"
PKG_BREW_NAME="freetype libpng libtiff zlib libjpeg-turbo webp harfbuzz"
PKG_TEST_HEADER="#include <ft2build.h>\n#include <png.h>\n#include <tiffio.h>\n#include <jpeglib.h>\n"
PKG_LIBS="-lfreetype -lpng16 -ltiff -lz -ljpeg -lbz2 -lwebp -lharfbuzz"
PKG_CFLAGS=""
```

as well as:

```
  PKG_CFLAGS=``/opt/homebrew/bin/pkg-config --cflags ${PKG_CONFIG_NAME}`
  PKG_LIBS=``/opt/homebrew/bin/pkg-config --libs ${PKG_CONFIG_NAME}`
  PKG_LIBS="$PKG_LIBS -ljpeg -lwebp"
```

to get it to compile.

Compilation also requires a full Xcode installation.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Request: allow user to specify Symbol font
description:
With the release of R 4.0.0, the default `x11()`, `png()`, `jpeg()`, `tiff()`, `bmp()`, `svg()`, `cairo_pdf()`, and `cairo_ps()` devices accept a `symbolfamily` argument to let the user change the font used for symbols in an image ([source](https://developer.r-project.org/Blog/public/2020/04/17/changes-to-symbol-fonts-for-cairo-graphics-devices/index.html)).

With Base R `png()`:
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)
library(scales)

greek <- as.data.frame(c("alpha", "beta", "gamma"))
names(greek) <- "greek"

p <- ggplot(greek, aes(x = greek, y = 1)) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(family = "Fira Sans", size = 16),
    axis.text.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(name = NULL, labels = label_parse())

ggsave(
  "greek_base.png",
  plot = p,
  device = png,
  width = 3, height = 1, dpi = 600,
  type = "cairo", symbolfamily = cairoSymbolFont("Fira Sans")
)
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-27 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

This gives this plot, withe the "Fira Sans" font used:
![greek_base](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17527594/131157860-cf82742e-c20d-4230-b736-0a393f6c8e71.png)

With `ragg::agg_png()`:
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)
library(scales)

greek <- as.data.frame(c("alpha", "beta", "gamma"))
names(greek) <- "greek"

p <- ggplot(greek, aes(x = greek, y = 1)) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(family = "Fira Sans", size = 16),
    axis.text.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(name = NULL, labels = label_parse())

ggsave(
  "greek_ragg.png", 
  plot = p, 
  device = ragg::agg_png,
  width = 3, height = 1, dpi = 600
)
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-27 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Which gives this plot, using the system default "Symbol" font:
![greek_ragg](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17527594/131157077-07866522-3e2d-46f7-8b14-f5cec29e88cb.png)

title: New format of calls to `agg_png` in `ggsave` break scaling function:
description:
Related to #66 - the updated format for calls of `agg_png` in `ggsave` breaks the `ggsave` code in @thomasp85's [plot scaling walkthrough](https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2020/08/taking-control-of-plot-scaling/).

These commands produce the same size/resolution image:
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)

p <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, col = Species)) + geom_point()

ggsave("test1.png",
       p,
       device = agg_png( 
       width = 10,
       height = 5, 
       units = "cm",
       scaling = 1,
       res = 200))
#> Saving 3.94 x 1.96 in image

ggsave("test2.png",
       p,
       device = agg_png( 
       width = 40,
       height = 20, 
       units = "cm",
       scaling = 4,
       res = 200))
#> Saving 3.94 x 1.97 in image
```

Whereas these work as expected (with same arguments outside of `ggsave`:
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)

p <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, col = Species)) + geom_point()


agg_png("test1.png", 
        width = 10,
        height = 5, 
        units = "cm",
        res = 200)
print(p)
dev.off()

agg_png("test2.png",
        width = 40, 
        height = 20,
        units = "cm", 
        res = 200,
        scaling = 4)
print(p)
dev.off()
```

i assume this is a font issue, but i'm finding under macOS that `ragg` does not display hebrew, japanese, characters, where as the default XQuartz renderer does. i.e.

title: Update documentation for agg_png with ggsave
description:
First time I've reported an issue, so please bare with me if I leave anything out.  The protocol for saving a plot with ggsave with device = agg_png seems to have changed, but not clearly communicated within documentation.  

previous example may be something like

`ggsave("mtcars.png", device = agg_png, res = 400)`

However, the working method now is 

`ggsave("mtcars.png", device = agg_png(res = 400))`

I like the change, but it does not seem to be documented anywhere, at least nowhere that I noticed.

title: Inverted raster images
description:
When displaying the background image in a ggplot using `annotation_custom()` and a rasterGrob, the image is inverted if the y-axis is reversed, but only when ragg is the graphics device. This doesn't happen with other graphics devices like quartz_png, which show the image upright. So the same code can produce different graphs depending on the render environment (e.g., knitr vs pkgdown).

See https://debruine.github.io/imginv/articles/test.html for a demonstration of the problem in situ.

This should reproduce the problem. 

```
library(ggplot2) # also uses functions from ragg and grid

# set up raster image and plot
grad <- matrix(hcl(seq(0, 280, 40), 80, 80), nrow=8, ncol=5)
img <- grid::rasterGrob(grad)
width <- 500
height <- 800

p <- ggplot() +
  scale_y_reverse() + # this is the problem
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, width),
              ylim = c(0, height)) +
  annotation_custom(img, 0, width, -height, 0) +
  geom_point(aes(x, y), data.frame(x = 0, y = 0))

# displays red on top - correct
# if your computer is different from mine, this might need to have another graphics device set
# but I don't know how to do that outside knitr options, quartz_png shows the image upright
p 

# displays purple on top
file <- tempfile(fileext='.png')
ragg::agg_png(file, width = width, height = height, res = 72)
p
dev.off()
browseURL(file)
```

title: Some shapefile polygons do not get printed correctly using  geom_sf and ragg together
description:
I ran into [this](https://github.com/r-spatial/sf/issues/1522) issue of not correctly rendering alpha levels using a combination of `geom_sf` and `coord_sf` on Windows machines. I thought I had solved that problem using ragg. However, using ragg a new problem came up. When I use ragg as graphics engine a transformed polygon does not render as expected (in fill the whole plot and not just the 'inside' of the polygon.




### Using the default graphic engine

This is the expected output.

```
library(rworldmap)
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(ragg)

polar_projection <- "+proj=stere +lat_0=90 +lat_ts=71 +lon_0=0 +k=1 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0"
World_map  <- getMap(resolution = "low")
World_map_transformed <- st_transform(st_as_sf(World_map),
                                      crs = polar_projection)

p1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = World_map_transformed,
          fill = "#eddfb7",
          col = "black")+
  coord_sf( xlim = c(-4500000, 4500000),
            ylim = c(-4500000, 4500000), expand = F) 

ggsave("regular_graph.png", p1)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18034318/97842490-97808880-1cdf-11eb-96d1-14c19e4a47bf.png)


### Using the RAGG graphic engine

The polygon fill does not work


```
agg_png("agg_graph.png", width = 700, height = 700, res = 144)
p1
invisible(dev.off())
```

title: CI issues due to new {text shaping} dependency
description:
Hi @thomasp85,

the new {ragg} release requires {textshaping} which again relies on system libs `harfbuzz` and `fribidi`.
Since {pkgdown} pull in {ragg}, the lack of the mentioned system libs breaks a lot of CI workflows ([example](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3spatiotempcv/runs/1212844810?check_suite_focus=true#step:12:2502))

I can adjust for this upstream in {tic} but many other users might eventually face issues as well. 
Can you let me know if this requirement will persist to prevent unneeded work? Thanks :)

title: particular detection of ggsave
description:
Hi, just a quick question, feel free to redirect me if there is a better place for that. I noticed this pattern:

```r
if (deparse(sys.call(), nlines = 1, width.cutoff = 500) == 'dev(filename = filename, width = dim[1], height = dim[2], ...)') {
  units <- 'in'
}
```
This essentially checks if somebody does this right?
```r
ggplot2::ggsave(
  ...,
  device = ragg::agg_png,
  ...
)
```
so for `ggsave`, the unit changes to inches rather than anything else. This deviates from the behavior of `ggplot2::ggsave(device = grDevices::png)`. Here `ggsave` recognizes a function, proceeds to do nothing, and saving is done using pixels (unlike when `device = "png"`).

A workaround is this:
```r
ggplot2::ggsave(
  ...,
  device = function(...) ragg::agg_png(...),
  ...
)
```
and then saving is still done using pixels.

My question is, why do you change the units to inches? ggsave also supports `cm` and `mm` (as does `ragg`) so those cannot be used anymore. I'm just curious about the idea behind this design choice, as this may impact how I can use `ragg` (e.g., probably without using `ggsave`).


For what it's worth, below an example that crashes `ggsave`  but not `ragg` as a consequence of this (which lead me to creating this issue):
```r
library(ragg)
library(ggplot2)
g <- qplot(rnorm(10), rnorm(10))
f <- tempfile()

# works
agg_png(filename = f, width = 1500, height = 1000, bg = "transparent", res = 225)
print(g)
dev.off()

# Error in dev(filename = filename, width = dim[1], height = dim[2], ...) : 
#   C++ exception: std::bad_alloc
ggsave(filename = f, width = 1500, height = 1000, device = agg_png, bg = "transparent", res = 225, limitsize = FALSE)

# actual call made by ggsave
# agg_png(filename = f, width = 1500, height = 1000, units = "in", bg = "transparent", res = 225)
```

title: Is platform-independent text a design goal?
description:
Just wondering whether you're planning to support pixel-perfect identical output across platforms in conjunction with the new textshaping package. I was hoping to build a visual difference tool to check output from my html rendering library, but outputs were different across OS X, Windows, and Linux. (I made sure to use the same fonts.) As far as I can tell, systemfonts and textshaping use whichever versions of harfbuzz and freetype2 are installed on the system, which will lead to version-dependent output just like it did with an early version of vdiffr.

Maybe this should be filed with systemfonts or textshaping or both? Related: Issue #28.

title: Can't call agg_png inside of a function
description:
See the code below; when I put agg_png inside of a function, if fails to render the plot. I'm guessing this has less to do with ragg and more with my understanding of functions or devices or....

(if the plot is `plot(sin, -pi, 2*pi)` instead of a ggplot, then it works)

```library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)

# this works
file <- "tempfile.png"
agg_png(file)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=hp, y=cyl)) + geom_point()
dev.off()


# embedding inside a function
plot_it <- function() {
  file <- "tempfile-func.png"
  agg_png(file)
  ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=hp, y=cyl)) + geom_point()
  dev.off()
}

# the plot is created, but it is empty
plot_it()
```

title: Slow rendering of png files (Linux)
description:
The following example
```
library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)
library(Cairo)
set.seed(1)
x = rnorm(1000); y = rnorm(1000)

g = ggplot(data.frame(x, y), aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 3, slope = 1, size = 3) +
  geom_label(x = 2.5, y = -1,
             label = "This is italic text\n in Arial Narrow",
             family = "Arial Narrow",
             fontface = "italic", size = 6, label.size = 0) +
  theme_bw(base_family = "Times") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "italic"),
        plot.title = element_text( face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "italic"),
        plot.caption = element_text(face = "plain")) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4)
```
Takes around 20 seconds using ragg
```
res = 300
system.time({
  ragg::agg_png("/tmp/tmp-ragg.png", width = 8 * res, height = 6 * res, res = res)
  print(g)
  dev.off()
})
```
But only  2 seconds using `png`
```
library(extrafont)
extrafont::loadfonts()
system.time({
  png("/tmp/tmp-cairo.png", type = "cairo-png", width = 8 * res, height = 6 * res, res = res)
  print(g)
  dev.off()
})
```
Your vignette on [performance](https://ragg.r-lib.org/articles/ragg_performance.html) mentions text performance with the comment "Ragg is slightly faster than Cairo", but the associated plot doesn't sure this.

title: agg_png() gives a warning when specifying all of width, height, units, and res
description:
This seems really odd, but `agg_png()` fails for me (with error message `the condition has length > 1`) when I specify a value for all of `width`, `height`, `units`, and `res`, but not if I leave out one of them.

Below is a reprex. Whenever the message is `"quartz_off_screen"` and there is no visible plot, the function worked. But when it fails for the last case, the plot appears here as it didn't go into a file.

``` r
library(ragg)

agg_png("foobar.png"); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2
agg_png("foobar.png", units = "px", res = 72); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2
agg_png("foobar.png", width = 480, height = 480); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2
agg_png("foobar.png", width = 480, height = 480, units = "px"); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2
agg_png("foobar.png", width = 480, height = 480, res = 72); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2
agg_png("foobar.png", width = 480, units = "px", res = 72); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2
agg_png("foobar.png", height = 480, units = "px", res = 72); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2
agg_png("foobar.png", width = 480, height = 480, units = "px", res = 72); plot(1:10); dev.off()
#> Error in if (deparse(sys.call()) == "dev(filename = filename, width = dim[1], height = dim[2], ...)") {: the condition has length > 1
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/xRwUFMZ.png)

    #> null device 
    #>           1

<sup>Created on 2019-07-15 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

**Edit:** `condition has length > 1` is of course normally a warning and not an error. I thought `reprex::reprex()` runs as vanilla, but apparently it obeys my `~/.Renviron` where I have this line:
`_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_CONDITION_ = true`. I updated the title of the issue, as the function does work, but just gives out a warning when all the listed parameters are specified in the function call.

title: Remove unnecessary null pointer checks
description: [An extra null pointer check is not needed](https://isocpp.org/wiki/faq/freestore-mgmt#delete-handles-null "Do I need to check for null before delete p?") in destructors like for the classes “[gradient_contour](https://github.com/thomasp85/ragg/blob/c72cf825c2b3ad0188be7e6264ccfa90e34ba553/src/agg/include/agg_span_gradient_contour.h#L77 "Destructor for gradient_contour")” and “[gradient_image](https://github.com/thomasp85/ragg/blob/c72cf825c2b3ad0188be7e6264ccfa90e34ba553/src/agg/include/agg_span_gradient_image.h#L92 "Destructor for gradient_image")”.
